cars.variant: S3 quattro — original spring 1999 Germany six-speed manual
cars.specification_market: First-generation Audi A3/S3 Type 8L sporting-road family, selected original spring 1999 German S3 six-speed manual. One family across 210 PS and later 225 PS versions, facelifts, equipment, years and regional names; no extra output or trim counts. Existing 8P/8V/8Y RS3 records are later A3 generations; no original 8L is present. Factory launch account preserved by Automotive Intelligence controls selected launch figures; Audi's 2026 generation account corroborates engine layout/twin intercoolers and 210 PS introduction. No engine code, exact cc, mass, maximum speed, brake dimensions, rear-disc ventilation or detailed fixed torque split imported. PistonHeads drove a later 225 PS MTM-tuned heritage car: its 250hp, measured performance and BAM details are not original 1999 specifications. Quattro here uses a hydraulic multi-plate clutch, not a longitudinal mechanical centre-differential system.
cars.summary: The original S3 established Audi's turbocharged, all-wheel-drive premium performance hatchback formula. Its lasting influence is documented in a retrospective drive and its original sporting-road character in a 1999 road test. Treat it as an influential hot hatch with reserved handling character, not as an unqualified handling benchmark; count the complete 8L sporting-road family once.

sources.title: Audi S3 — original spring 1999 German launch account
sources.notes: Complete relevant launch body read through German spring-1999 availability paragraph. Preserved text matches the separately indexed February-1999 Audi release on AudiWorld; the AudiWorld full page returned 403 and is not claimed as read. Sixteen attributes use this launch narrative; engine layout and twin intercoolers map to source 1. The linked technical sheet points to an A6 path and is not used. No top speed, exact cc, engine code, mass or rear-disc ventilation imported. Retain 154 kW rather than copying its ambiguous 210 bhp label; Audi source 1 confirms 210 PS.

sources.title: 30 Jahre Audi A3: Drei Jahrzehnte Vorsprung im Premium-Kompaktsegment — 9 October 2026, first-generation section
sources.notes: Introduction, complete first-generation 8L section, later-generation distinctions and chronology read. Two engine attributes map here: inline-four configuration and turbo with two intercoolers. Confirms original S3 154 kW/210 PS, manual six-speed, three doors, and later 165 kW/225 PS update. Does not assign five-door A3 body to S3. No rear-ventilated-disc claim or figures from later A3/RS3 generations imported.

sources.title: Audi S3 — Trygve Bæra, 3 April 1999; first published BIL 4/1999
sources.notes: Complete original review body and panel read. Describes six-speed gearbox operation and successful balance of sporting chassis and comfort over uneven roads. German April availability and Norwegian June arrival are distinguished. Supplies contemporary admission context only; no numerical specifications imported. Apparent wheelbase-unit error in panel, driver-inclusive mass and later brake conflicts are not reused.

sources.title: Audi S3 | PH Origin Story — Matt Bird, 24 July 2022
sources.source_type: Original retrospective drive of modified heritage car with historical analysis
sources.notes: Complete feature body and both specification panels read. Documents influence on the premium AWD turbo hot-hatch formula, secure character and heavy/numb steering, rather than a universal handling-win claim. Actual old car is an MTM demonstrator retained in modified tune from a later 225 PS base; 250hp, 273lb-ft, 6.0-second and BAM details are not stock 1999 specifications despite its panel heading. Embedded quotations from period magazines are secondary reporting, not independently read original tests. No technical attribute maps here.
